items.name: Blog: What is an Outcome?
items.postCopy: Walk into any meeting and ask three people what an "outcome" is, and you'll get three very different answers. As an Outcome-Based Services provider for over 13 years, it's one of the most common questions we still get, and one worth answering precisely, because the word gets used to mean almost anything. For us, an outcome has four components: a business result the customer cares about, a number you can put against it, attribution to specific work, and a deadline. If any one of those is missing, you don't have an outcome. You have a hope. We break down the difference between outcomes, outputs, and deliverables in our latest blog.

items.name: Blog: The Customer is the Only Metric that Matters
items.postCopy: Behind every technology project is a person who vouched for it. Someone who stood in front of a board or a room of skeptical peers and said, 'Trust me, this will work.' That person is spending something that never shows up in a budget: their credibility. Our outcome-based services model is built around protecting that credibility, by tying a provider's success directly to the customer's business results, not just hours billed or deliverables shipped. The customer is the only metric that matters. Everything else is a means to that end.
